newsitem.title: USA: Coastal's ANR Pipeline announces open season.
newsitem.headline: Coastal's ANR Pipeline announces open season.

text.p: Coastal Corp's ANR Pipeline Co (ANR) on Wednesday announced an open season for transportation of natural gas from the Chicago supply hub to any delivery point in Wisconsin from November 1998.
- The open season to begin immediately and conclude July 21, 1997.
- ANR later this summer will file for approval with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to construct facilities necessary to accommodate requests received during the open season.
- Pending FERC approval, ANR anticipates construction in the summer of 1998 for service beginning Nov. 1, 1998.
"Existing capacity from Chicago to Wisconsin is about 1.1 billion cubic feet (per day), and it's basically all spoken for," a company spokesman told Reuters.
The company said nominations for 1999 already totaled 500 million cubic feet per day above existing capacity.

"ANR's open season for service commencing in 1999 is unaffected. ANR is holding this open season in response to requests for service beginning in 1998," Jeffrey Connelly, president of ANR Pipeline Company, said in the statement.

Since expansion of facilities was necessary for services requested by customers in 1999, ANR wanted to give all shippers an opportunity to commence service in 1998 by constructing the facilities earlier, Connelly said.

As a result of the expedited program, ANR will be able to provide more gas transportation capacity to serve Wisconsin sooner, while maximizing the use of existing local distribution company infrastructure, minimizing costs for consumers.

Shippers interested in acquiring five-year contracts for the 10-cent firm transportation service, which includes an option for 100-day storage service, should contact Lee Bennett at 414-547-5528 or Bob MacMillan at 313-496-3814.
Requests for service and a $10,000 deposit must be received by July 21, 1997.
ANR Pipeline Co is a Detroit-based interstate pipeline subsidiary of the Coastal Corp.
ANR operates a 10,500-mile interstate natural gas pipeline system providing storage, transportation and capacity-related services for lusers and other customers in the U.S. and Canada.
